llm.summary: This skill can use a logged-in browser to save or publish CSDN articles after automatically modifying their content, including adding a configured WeChat QR section and potentially removing trailing content after a matching heading.

dimensions.detail: Use of a persistent local Edge or Chrome profile and existing CSDN login is purpose-aligned for browser publishing, but it grants account-level draft and publication authority and saves screenshots in the working directory.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer, dependency-fetch step, service, or scheduled persistence was found, but the config includes a user-specific install path and a packaged promotional QR URL/description.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents draft, preview, and publish modes, but the script has no enforced final confirmation or content diff before clicking publish controls, and it exposes broad file path, browser, profile, and article-id arguments.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no OS-level backdoor or startup persistence, but the default keeps the authenticated browser session open and reuses the user's persistent browser profile, increasing the impact of mistaken or unintended publication.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Publishing Markdown to CSDN through an authenticated browser is coherent with the stated purpose, but the script unconditionally appends or replaces a WeChat public-account section using packaged configuration, which is not necessary to the core publishing task and affects user-authored content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Use only with a browser profile and CSDN account you are comfortable granting publication access to, inspect the generated article before publishing, and remove or change the packaged WeChat QR configuration if it is not yours. Avoid publish mode until the skill adds an explicit final confirmation and non-destructive content diff.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced script is present in the artifact and was inspected in full, so the partial-inspection concern is downgraded as a scanner coverage issue rather than artifact behavior.
[LP3] expected: Browser automation and local file reading are expected for this skill, but the artifact does not declare a minimal permission/tool scope despite using a logged-in browser profile.
[SQP-2] expected: Publish mode is part of the stated function, but the implementation directly clicks confirmation-style publish buttons without an independent human confirmation gate.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language instructions fit a CSDN publishing workflow and are not a security concern by themselves.
[T01] unexpected: The content-mutation finding is supported: the script always calls the WeChat-section append/replace logic, and matching an existing heading causes the article from that heading onward to be replaced before draft save or publish.
